title: Why I Like Building Things
subtitle: Turning curiosity into small pieces of the internet.
content: Over the past few years, I’ve realized that most meaningful things in life come from building – sometimes software, sometimes ideas, and sometimes just habits that slowly shape who you become. When I write code, I’m not only solving a technical problem. I’m trying to create something that didn’t exist before: a tool, a system, a small piece of the internet that someone might find useful. There’s something deeply satisfying about turning curiosity into something real.

A lot of my projects start in a very simple way. A question, a random idea, or a small frustration. What if this process was automated? What if this dataset could tell a story? What if an AI agent could actually do something useful instead of just answering questions? From there, it becomes a process of experimenting, breaking things, rebuilding them, and learning along the way. Most things don’t work the first time, but that’s part of the fun.

This website is a small collection of those explorations. Some projects are polished, others are rough prototypes, and a few are just experiments that taught me something new. But each one represents a moment of curiosity and the willingness to try building something anyway. If something here sparks an idea for you, then it’s already done its job.
